answer: Anchor each agent identity to a single on-chain stake that decays slowly, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up many identities. Like timber in a house frame, reputation accrues only through completed work verified by peers over time, making a fresh Sybil account structurally weak. When agents trade, payments flow along a vine of past successful collaborations, so a new identity with no history earns little and must invest real effort before it can extract value, raising the attacker cost far above any gain.
